title: Staged integration lanes for bespoke on-prem networking requests
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting private/VPC/on-prem deployments vary widely in network topology, security posture, and upgrade constraints. Our current intake funnels too many bespoke requests into manual engineering triage which increases lead time and unpredictable SLAs.

Goal: Design a staged integration lanes system that classifies incoming on-prem/VPC/air-gapped requests into three operational lanes (self-serve, assisted-template, bespoke-concierge). Each lane has clear entry gates, required customer commitments (operator tasks), and a bounded SLO for time-to-ready. The system should reduce manual touchpoints for common patterns while making bespoke work predictable and measurable.

Scope: Networking and upgrade constraints only (connectivity, egress policy, bastion/proxy patterns, OS/container images, air-gap patching). Excludes billing/contracting, infra procurement, and model compatibility validation.

Constraints and assumptions: customers have a solutions engineering contact; we can require a short preflight agent/probe to collect telemetry; legal/regulatory variance will be handled outside lane assignment and routed as compliance block.

Key outputs: triage rubric, preflight probe checklist, lane-specific runbooks (including temporary bastion templates and automated rollback steps), customer-facing intake form fields, and a priority SLA matrix for each lane.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic rubric maps >90% of historical on-prem requests into one of the three lanes without manual override
A one-page customer intake form (Drive link) captures all data points required for lane assignment
Assisted-template lane has two reusable network templates (bastion-based proxy & reverse-tunnel) with documented operator steps and estimated engineering effort <= 3 days
Bespoke-concierge lane runbook includes risk assessment checklist, minimum operator commitments, and a measurable timeline with agreed checkpoints (kickoff, readiness probe, final validation)
Dashboard track: mean time from intake to 'ready-for-onboarding' per lane and reduction in manual triage tickets by 40% in first quarter after rollout
comments: 2026-03-05 Maya Rodriguez: Drafted initial problem statement after reviewing last quarter's onboarding backlog and SE notes. Noticed ~48% of tickets were network-related bespoke asks.

2026-03-06 Liam Chen: Engineering flagged kernel version compatibility as a recurring blocker; added to gate checklist. Suggested adding an 'unsupported config' quick-decline path to avoid open-ended work.

decisions: Adopt three-lane model: self-serve (templated network + allowed egress), assisted-template (SE-assisted with operator tasks), bespoke-concierge (full engineering engagement)
Require a lightweight preflight probe as a mandatory gate for assisted-template and bespoke lanes; self-serve must pass a basic checklist before commit
Temporary bastion proxy pattern is preferred default for customers unwilling/unable to open egress; we will provide templated deployment artifacts (Ansible + Docker)
Introduce a 'decline with reason' outcome for configurations that pose unacceptable risk (unsupported hypervisor, obsolete OS, regulatory constraints outside product scope)
Create explicit operator commitment checklist that customers sign (maintenance window, patching cadence, access window) before scheduling engineering work
risks: Customers may under-report network constraints on intake form causing downstream rework
Security/Compliance exceptions could push work from assisted to bespoke lane unexpectedly
Engineering capacity shortage for bespoke lane could create long SLAs if not strictly gated
metrics: Percent of requests auto-classified by rubric
Mean time (days) from intake to 'ready-for-onboarding' by lane
Number of manual engineering touchpoints per request
